assets.label: Contact shadow — soft ground occlusion blob
assets.notes: AMBIENT OCCLUSION, NOT A CAST SHADOW. Non-directional on purpose: it is the darkening where an object occludes ambient light at its base, so it is correct at every time of day and does NOT need redoing when a sun direction is chosen. Raheem, 2026-08-07, worried a shadow would have to change once time-of-day is picked — this one will not. Cast shadows are a separate, later, directional asset. Reusable under any building or prop; scale to the object's width.

assets.label: Tan kerb (plain, darker) — wang 32
assets.notes: Raheem, 2026-08-07: the tan+white brick should be the ROAD; the kerb should be 'a solid or darker tan block, not white and tan spotted'. So this is the same brick with the cream speckle removed (543 px above luma 195 mapped to base tan rgb(197,150,106)) and darkened to 0.70 — mortar only to 0.90, else the kerb becomes a black grid. Road/kerb luma gap 153 -> 104 = 49. Zero generations. A grey-stone recolour was tried first and rejected: 'I actually like the colour of the tan bricks.'

assets.label: The Forge — exterior, PixelLab redraw (v2)
assets.notes: THE QUALITY FIX. v1 was Gemini art box-downsampled: measured 0.6% flatness and 26,393 colours — a photo shrunk down, not pixel art, which is why it read soft beside the kit. v2 feeds the ORIGINAL 942px Gemini crop to PixelLab POST /image-to-pixelart (first ever use of that endpoint in this project; 1 generation) which REDRAWS it. Then: white keyed by border flood, ground cut at row 187 (ground share jumped 16%->60%), fabric quantized to 40 colours, and the portal given its OWN 24-colour ramp so the rainbow is not starved by the stone. Result 64 colours, 42.9% flatness, saturation 58.4. Castle wall reference is 48 colours / 59.4%.

assets.label: The Forge — portal glow, separate layer
assets.notes: The doorway vortex on its own layer so it can be lit independently during the walk-into-the-forge transition, and so it does not compete with the stone for palette slots. Ellipse centre (143,160) r 27x24 in the 320x200 redraw.

assets.label: The Archivist — exterior, PixelLab redraw (v2)
assets.notes: Same pipeline as castle.forge.v2. Original 941px Gemini crop -> POST /image-to-pixelart (1 gen, $0.0100) -> white keyed by border flood -> ground cut at row 264 (ground share 42%->64%) -> quantized to 48 colours -> dehalo. NO protected glow region here, unlike the forge: 46.5% of this building is above saturation 60 because the blue stone and teal dome ARE the building, so a saturation split would have bucketed half the facade as glow. Straight quantize 48 measured better anyway: flatness 37.4%->64.7%, 48 colours, only -7% saturation. Castle wall reference is 48 colours / 59.4% flatness.
